text:
sam: Pushed PR #46211 that refactors the batching scheduler to support adaptive windowing. It's small but touches runtime batch loop + platform routing. Asking for runtime, infra, security eyes before I merge tomorrow morning.
lee: Link? Can you paste the PR and a short summary of the risk and test plan?
sam: https://github.com/redwood-inference/repo/pull/46211 — main risk: off-by-one in window math that could increase latency spikes. Tests: unit + loadbench in staging + kv-cache smoke. Rollout: canary 5% then 25%.
nina (Runtime): I'll take a look later today. If it's only window logic and you have staging loadbench data, ping me with the perf graph.
priya (Eng-Infra): Need to confirm eviction interplay — does this change pointer to prefetcher? If so, we should schedule a small capacity test on stage GPUs.
alex (Security): Quick Q: any new env vars or KMS calls? If not, we can skip full security review; else tag me.
sam: No new KMS, only scheduler params. I attached perf graphs: https://redwood-internal/graphs/pr-46211. Staging qps looks fine, tail latency improved at 95th but 99th bumped slightly — investigating.
ci-bot: CI passed: unit(12/12), integration(8/8), e2e(2/2)
lee: Can you add a fallback flag and a rollout plan in PR? If runtime needs to revert, we want a fast feature flag.
sam: Added flag + rollback steps in PR description.
nina (Runtime): Skimmed the diff — mostly good. Two comments inline about atomic update of window size. If you can address, I can LGTM by EOD.
priya (Eng-Infra): Scheduling a quick 30m capacity test at 10:30 PT tomorrow — cc @oncall-sre. If results look good, infra can OK staging canary.
alex (Security): No blockers from sec.
sam: thanks all — aiming to merge 11:00 PT after canary owners confirm. Will post merge note.
lee: :thumbsup:
sam: Merge note: merged at 11:05 PT — canary at 5% rolling now.
ops-bot: Canary rollout started: pr-46211 -> canary 5%
nina (Runtime): Seeing no regressions in canary. Increase to 25% in 15m?
sam: bumping to 25% now.
ops-bot: Canary update: 25% complete.
sam: closing thread, thanks.
